noi_dung:
Cultivators Must Not Lie

In the Chan Hall, we must follow the Chan Hall's rules—no maverick acts of our own. Remember: the Chan Hall trains sages—never wreck the Way-place, costing others their chance at enlightenment. On this point, Session participants must take special heed—guarding the precepts strictly, never lightly.

Joining a Chan Session is a rare affinity—a thousand myriads of times not to be wasted. Now we gather here investigating Chan together through good roots of past lives, leading to today's affinity. The cultivator of the Way, meeting this chance, must seize enlightenment's moment—wasting no time, not a second or minute. Never for momentary pleasure seek comfort in laziness—for that wastes enlightenment's chance and may plunge you into the three evil destinies. Then regret comes too late. Hence my two lines:

Do not wait for suffering to study the Way; the three evil destinies are all lazy people.

These two lines mean: do not wait for suffering to seek the Way. Beings in the three evil destinies (hells, hungry ghosts, animals) are all lazy people.

So the meditator must apply effort hour after hour, ever vigorous. The hua-tou ever in mind—walking also investigating, sitting also investigating—investigating back and forth, investigating penetratingly—and the original face appears. Why? Because the hua-tou can smash discursive thoughts. Investigate until above, you know no sky; below, you know no earth; between, you know no people—then when would discursive thoughts arise? Understand that discursive thoughts are precisely false speech—that is, we fail the five basic precepts: through rivalry we lie, through greed we lie, through seeking we lie, through selfishness we lie, through self-benefit we lie. Lying to deceive others, erring yet never admitting, finding excuses for ourselves—with such thoughts and acts, how cultivate the Way?

Why does our effort show no progress? Precisely because we have lied too much. One lie breeds a hundred discursive thoughts. Then sitting—sitting unseated; standing—standing unsteady—the illness of restlessness, not knowing how to bear oneself—advance or retreat? Which is right? Which is wrong? No peace to be found—wholly against the Dharma.

The true cultivator, everywhere follows the rules, ever vigorous—never speaking falsehood, never drifting with whatever comes. May we imitate no liars, follow none who flout the rules—for following them brings no benefit but harm. Take care on this point, take heed—lest infection bring great calamity.

The true cultivator fears no suffering, shrinks from no hardship—hour after hour, minute after minute strictly cultivating, unmoved by outer states.

Investigate! Investigate! Investigate! Investigate until waters recede and rocks appear—seeing clearly the original face.
